newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals-Copper, zinc seen enlivening market.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals-Copper, zinc seen enlivening market.

text.p: Copper and zinc are expected to breathe some life into a dull metals market this week ahead of India's fiscal budget for 1997/98 (April/March), dealers said on Wednesday.

They said the local non-ferrous metals market had not yet picked up despite a firm trend on the London Metals Exchange (LME). India imports most non-ferrous metals, the cost of which depends on price movements on the LME.
In the week to Wednesday, all base metals except copper and zinc remained steady in dull trade.
Copper gained 250 rupees per quintal (100 kgs) to 12,850 and zinc rose 50 rupees to 6,800 rupees per quintal.
"LME is going strong. But the local market has not picked up as much as it should mainly because of sluggish industrial demand," said leading metals dealer Jashubhai Gangadas Mehta.
He said local traders also faced a liquidity crunch, some of them having run up losses because of price fluctuations on the LME in the last few months.
Mehta said copper prices had fallen steeply by 45/49 rupees per kg since October/November last year in deals they had struck when LME prices were high.
Copper prices had since improved marginally but poor local demand did not help much, he said.
"Demand for copper can improve only after the national budget," Mehta said. The 1997/98 fiscal budget is scheduled for presentation in parliament on February 28.
Dealers feel the budget may not bring them enough relief as import tariffs are expected to be lowered further in line with the liberal image the government seeks to project.

Industry and trade have been demanding that uniform import tariffs on semi-finished products and raw materials have not helped domestic industry. They have urged the government to fix a differential of 15 percent between the two categories.
"At present people do not want to import, do not want to trade and do not want to keep stocks," Mehta said.
Copper and zinc, however, are likely to stay firm on account of a shortage.
Dealers said the state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL), which raised zinc prices by 1,500 rupees per tonne this month, is expected to raise them again by another 3,000 rupees per tonne in February.
They said another state-run company, the Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL), may also raise its prices by 5,000 rupees per tonne in the next few days to catch up with the LME trend.
